userStories.title: A run chief itself calls quiet is not also called stalled
userStories.description:
`⚠ stalled — no activity for N` is derived from LOG WRITES, not from run state, so it fires on states where silence is the expected, correct behaviour — and it does so on the SAME LINE where chief has already printed the reason for that silence. The two halves of the line contradict each other, which trains an operator to ignore a flag that should mean something.

MEASURED 2026-08-13, two independent cases:

1. **rate-limited** — ten tasklists across three repos read `rate-limited-waiting for 16m · ⚠ stalled — no activity for 16m`. chief KNOWS it is rate-limited; it printed that itself, from the same `live_note()` call that then appended the stall marker. All three driver processes were alive (`S+`), nothing was wedged, and every one resumed when the usage window reopened.
2. **long buffered gate** — `cuneiform:314` ran `⚠ stalled — no activity for 36m` while `cargo test` was working normally. Sampling the child PID showed the test binary CHANGING between samples (`render_oauth_session_gate` → `render_offline_walker`): real forward progress, invisible because a non-tty `cargo test` block-buffers its output.

The fix is local: `live_note()` (`engine/monitor.sh` ~line 169) already holds `$phase` in a variable at the exact point it appends the marker on ~line 175.
acceptanceCriteria: The stall marker is NOT appended for a phase where quiet is the expected behaviour — at minimum `rate-limited-waiting`, and the phase list is data (one place to add a state), not a condition repeated at both call sites (`engine/monitor.sh` ~175 and ~519 both render it).

A test drives `live_note()` over a synthetic live-file for each known phase and asserts which do and do not gain the marker — so 'which states are exempt' is checkable rather than a reading of the shell.
The exemption is NOT unconditional silence: see US-2. A state that is quiet for a legitimate reason still becomes noteworthy eventually, and this story must not make it permanently unflaggable.
`bin/chief ps` and `bin/chief monitor` are both checked, since the two call sites render the flag differently (one via `live_note … stale`, one via a bare fallback string).

`provider-waiting` is classified explicitly and the classification is justified: it is NOT quiet-by-design like `rate-limited-waiting`, because a provider that never returns is a real hang. It takes a long threshold under US-2 rather than an exemption. Two runs on 2026-08-17 sat in this phase having produced 0 bytes and never reached iteration 1 — the case an exemption would hide.
userStories.notes: test/stall-flag.sh: PASS — 5 quiet-by-design phases unflagged and 36 flagged at 40m of silence, drift guard over all 39 phase literals engine/*.sh publishes, ceiling case (6h40m quiet) flags; chief ps AND chief monitor both green. Negative control (CHIEF_STALE_QUIET_SECONDS=900) fails the test as expected. bash -n clean on bin/chief + engine/*.sh + install.sh + test/*.sh + templates/*.sh; test/liveliness.sh, test/monitor.sh, test/limitmonitor.sh, test/doc-sync.sh: 4/4 green.

userStories.title: The threshold is per-phase, because forever is still wrong
userStories.description: Suppressing the flag outright would replace a false positive with a blind spot: a rate limit that never clears, or a provider wait that has genuinely hung, is exactly what an operator needs told. What is wrong today is the THRESHOLD, not the concept — 15 minutes is alarming for an agent turn and unremarkable for a usage window.
acceptanceCriteria: Each phase carries its own staleness threshold, with the DEFAULT unchanged so no existing behaviour moves for phases nobody re-tuned.

A quiet-by-design phase (`rate-limited-waiting`) gets a threshold long enough that a normal window reopen never trips it, and the chosen figure is justified in a comment against a measurement rather than picked round — the observed waits tonight were 5–16 minutes and resolved on their own.
A phase that exceeds its own threshold STILL flags, and the message says which state it was stuck in ('rate-limited for 2h') rather than the generic 'no activity', so the flag carries the diagnosis.

Liveness is checked before flagging where it is cheap to do so: a driver whose pid is gone is a DIFFERENT and more serious condition than a quiet one, and today both render as the same yellow note. If that check is not landed here, it is recorded as the follow-up rather than left implicit.
`shellcheck` (or the repo's existing shell lint) passes on `engine/monitor.sh`, and `.chief/verify.sh` is green.
userStories.notes: `.chief/verify.sh`: OK (allowing merge), exit 0 — quality ratchet ok (max_nesting_depth 5->5 delta 0; function_length_max 177->192 delta +15, tol 15 — render() is AT the edge), bash -n, VERSION-bump policy, behavioural bystander subset, doc-sync, tasklist jq all green. shellcheck 0.11.0 -S error on engine/monitor.sh + test/stall-flag.sh: CLEAN (run via `npx --yes shellcheck`; brew install cannot write /opt/homebrew here, so verify.sh's own shellcheck step self-skipped). test/stall-flag.sh: PASS, 5 parts, 3/3 consecutive runs green — every non-exempt phase asserted at its OWN threshold +/-60s, verifying/warmup pinned at 3060s, provider-waiting at the 900s default, flag text asserted to name the state and its limit ('stalled in rate-limited-waiting ... past its 6h30m limit'), dead-worker truth table (no pid / live pid / dead+verdict = not dead; dead+no verdict = gone) and both chief ps and chief monitor rendering the ✗ row. 3 negative controls each FAIL as expected: re-tune removed, dead-detection disabled, generic message restored. test/liveliness.sh, test/monitor.sh, test/limitmonitor.sh, test/doc-sync.sh: 4/4 PASS.

userStories.title: Elapsed-in-phase is shown routinely, not only when something is flagged
acceptanceCriteria: `chief ps` and `chief monitor` show how long the current phase has been held, beside the phase. US-2 already puts the duration in the FLAG message; this puts it in the ordinary view, which is where an operator decides whether to wait or intervene — and is the single line that would have resolved 2026-08-17 immediately.

The duration comes from the live-file's existing timestamps rather than a new clock, so a phase that has not been re-stamped reads as long-held instead of as fresh. A duration derived from the render time would show every run as instantaneous.

It renders in both call sites (`engine/monitor.sh` ~175 and ~519), which US-1 already notes diverge — a duration that appears in one view and not the other reproduces the current problem for whichever half an operator happens to be reading.

A run whose driver pid is GONE is visually distinct from one that is merely quiet. US-2 records this as landing here or as an explicit follow-up; either way the two must not render identically, because on 2026-08-17 nine runs were killed on the assumption they were the same thing.
userStories.notes: test/stall-flag.sh: PASS, 6 parts — part 6 drives all five row arms (live_note · limit_note · op_note · hold_note x2) and asserts each shows its OWN elapsed-in-phase (40m / 25m / 1h01m / 3h10m / 13m, no two alike) in chief ps AND chief monitor, on a FRESH heartbeat (rows read `for 40m ... 1s ago`) so the duration provably comes from phase_since and not the render clock; part 5 additionally pins the `gone` row LABEL. 3 negative controls each FAIL as expected: gone-label reverted, hold_note elapsed removed, live_phase_age re-pointed at heartbeat. .chief/verify.sh: OK (allowing merge), exit 0 — quality ratchet ok (function_length_max 177->180 delta +3 tol 15, max_nesting_depth 5->5, single_use_functions 13->14 tol 2). test/liveliness.sh, test/monitor.sh, test/limitmonitor.sh, test/overlap-zones.sh, test/plan-review.sh, test/doc-sync.sh: green.

userStories.title: `stalled` is a statement about NOW, not about the last iteration
userStories.description:
`agent.sh:868` sets `phase=stalled` at an iteration boundary when that iteration advanced neither a passing story nor HEAD. The stall COUNT is correct there and is the budget mechanism — leave it alone. The PHASE is not: it persists as the displayed phase for the whole of the NEXT iteration, so a run doing real work reads `stalled` until it happens to advance a counter.

Measured 2026-08-17. Tasklist 99 showed `phase: stalled` for ~25 minutes while it was in fact re-engaging after a post-rebase verify failure, fixing a quality-ratchet regression, and merging (it landed as e6826b1, 4/4 stories). Tasklist 98 showed `phase: stalled` with a 2-second heartbeat — actively working, correctly heartbeating, wrongly labelled. An operator watching either one sees the word chief uses for 'give up on this'.

The heartbeat is NOT the defect and must not be 'fixed': it was updating correctly in both cases. Only the phase string is wrong.
acceptanceCriteria: The next iteration's first `live_set` moves `phase` off `stalled` — a turn that has begun is an `agent-turn`, whatever the previous iteration did or did not advance.

The stall COUNT still persists across the boundary and still ends the run at `$STALL_LIMIT`. A test asserts a run that stalls twice in a row still stops, so the fix cannot buy legibility with a budget leak.
A behavioural test drives two consecutive no-progress iterations and asserts the phase reads `agent-turn` WHILE the second is running and `stalled` only between them.
`chief monitor` distinguishes 'no progress last iteration (n/N)' from 'not doing anything', in words an operator can act on. The first is normal; the second is the one worth stopping.
Re-engagement after a failed post-rebase verify — the driver's `persisted for re-engagement` path — reports itself as such rather than inheriting whatever phase the previous attempt left behind.
userStories.notes: test/stall-flag.sh: PASS, 9 parts — part 8 drives agent.sh through two consecutive no-progress iterations (fake provider on PATH, STALL_LIMIT=2, no driver) and the record's polled transcript reads `agent-turn provider-waiting agent-turn stalled integrating agent-turn provider-waiting agent-turn stalled integrating`: both provider turns ran under provider-waiting and both boundary-hook samples under `integrating`, never `stalled`, while the budget still ended the run — exit 1 at iteration 2 with stall=2, stall_limit=2, terminal phase `stalled`. Part 7 renders the two findings apart in BOTH views (`no progress last iter (2/2)` · `(1/5)` · `(2)` for an older record with no budget, vs `⚠ stalled in provider-waiting — no activity for 40m, past its 15m limit`). Part 9's two-run hermetic driver fixture: run 1 leaves VERIFY-FAILED, run 2 emits tasklist.re-engaged with detail 'every story passes but the branch failed verify post-rebase last run'. 5 negative controls each FAIL as expected (hook phase removed; the iteration's first live_set removed; bare 'stall N' restored — that one also fails test/liveliness.sh; mark_reengage removed; stall_limit never published). .chief/verify.sh: OK (allowing merge), exit 0 — quality ratchet ok (function_length_max 509->519 delta +10 tol 15; max_nesting_depth 6->6; single_use_functions 47->48 tol 2; duplicate_blocks 0->0), bash -n clean, VERSION-bump 0.8.57 covers every engine/bin change, behavioural bystander subset 34/34 PASS, DOC-SYNC PASS (README states v0.8.57), tasklist jq ok. test/events.sh and test/liveliness.sh: PASS. shellcheck 0.11.0 -S error on the 7 changed shell files: clean (the SC1072/SC1073 errors it reports in bin/chief + engine/quality.sh reproduce unchanged on main).

description:
🔴 **chief flags a run as stalled for being quiet in states where quiet is what it is supposed to look like — and gives an operator no way to tell slow from stuck.**

**Measured 2026-08-17.** Nine runs were stopped as 'stalled'. Seven were working: logs of 73KB, 47KB and 21KB at iterations 1–2, no limit hits, nothing wrong. They looked stalled because `chief monitor` showed `provider-waiting` and never changed, and there was no elapsed time beside it to say whether that meant *forty seconds into a turn* or *forty minutes into nothing*.

**`provider-waiting` is the whole duration of every agent turn.** `agent.sh:713` sets it immediately before invoking the provider CLI and it holds until the provider returns. It is not an error, and it is not counted as a stall — `stall=$((stall+1))` fires only at an iteration boundary with no new passing story and no new commit (`agent.sh:846`). So the phase label and the stall counter measure different things, and the display shows the one that cannot progress.

⚠️ **`provider-waiting` must NOT be exempted the way `rate-limited-waiting` is.** A rate-limit wait is quiet by design and resolves itself. A provider that never returns is a real hang, and two of the nine runs produced **0 bytes and never reached iteration 1** — the only genuine anomalies of the set. Exempting the phase would make exactly that case invisible. It needs a LONG threshold, which US-2's per-phase design already provides, not an exemption.

The diagnosis cost about an hour and three wrong theories — rate limits (the 429s were from logs days old), the provider (only one repo was even on Devin), and the installed-version gap. Every one of those would have been a glance if the display carried elapsed-in-phase.
